answers.d01: 似然回答的是：固定手上这批数据，哪个假设让它出现的可能性更大？注意方向：似然是 P(数据|参数)——给定假设算数据的概率；后验是 P(参数|数据)——看到数据后反过来问假设本身为真的概率。方向不能混。抛一枚硬币10次出9次正面：若假设正面概率0.5，这批数据出现的概率是 C(10,9)×0.5¹⁰≈0.0098；若假设正面概率0.9，则是 C(10,9)×0.9⁹×0.1≈0.387。0.9 的似然大得多，说明数据更支持它。但『0.9 为真』的后验还要再算一步：把似然乘上先验（你对这枚硬币的初始判断），再归一化。如果这枚硬币是从银行取的普通硬币，先验强烈偏向0.5，后验就不会跟着似然跑那么远。一句话：似然是数据给各假设打的分，后验是看完得分、连先验一起折算后的胜率；似然大只说明数据偏向它，不等于证实。
answers.d02: The average alone hides spread: {50, 50} and {0, 100} both average 50, but the second set is far more scattered. Population variance measures that spread: the average of squared distances from the mean, σ² = (1/N)·Σ(xᵢ − μ)². Why squared? Plain deviations always cancel to zero — that's just what the mean means — so squaring makes every gap count positively, and it weights large gaps more heavily, which is usually the point: one wildly off value matters more than two slightly off ones. Run it: for {0, 100}, deviations are −50 and +50, squares are 2500 each, variance = 2500. Note the unit is squared (square dollars); take the square root, σ = 50, to get back to dollars — that's the standard deviation. Move any point further from the mean and variance only rises. If your numbers are a sample rather than the whole population, divide by N−1 instead.
answers.d03: 正反馈是输出回到输入、并沿同一方向加强输入的回路：变化本身成为下一步变化的原因，所以被一轮轮放大。麦克风靠近音箱就是看得见的例子：话筒拾到声音，音箱放大播出，播出的又被拾到，啸叫越来越响。为什么放大：每一轮都以上一轮的结果为起点继续加码，没有环节把它往回拉。但放大是方向，不是评价。降价→顾客增多→单位成本下降→可以再降价，这也是正反馈，却是良性循环；银行挤兑、设备啸叫是同方向回路，却是灾难。可见『正』指自增强，好坏取决于被放大的是什么。现实中的放大也有限度：信号饱和、资金耗尽、顾客总量见顶，都会让回路最终停住。换到社交媒体同理：转发越多越被推荐，被推荐又带来更多转发，平台要做的正是给这个回路装上刹车。
answers.d04: Opportunity cost is the value of the single best option you give up — not all the options. A free afternoon: you could nap, hike, or study for an exam. Say hiking gives enjoyment worth 8, studying is worth 7, napping 3. If you hike, the opportunity cost is 7 — the best forgone choice, studying — not 8 plus 7 plus 3. Nothing here needs money; it's the benefit of the road not taken, and it exists even when the afternoon is free, which is exactly when people forget it. Now change one condition: if the exam moves to tomorrow morning, studying's value jumps to 12. Same afternoon, same options, but the cost of hiking just rose, so the sensible choice can flip. For any decision, the question is the same: what is the best thing I'm saying no to?
answers.d05: 检测报告『阳性』，你真正想知道的是 P(患病|阳性)——阳性条件下患病的概率。但检测说明书给的是反方向的数字：灵敏度 P(阳性|患病)=0.99，假阳性率 P(阳性|没病)=0.05。条件方向反了，不能把0.99直接当成患病把握。贝叶斯公式做的就是换方向：P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病) / P(阳性)，其中 P(阳性) 是阳性总占比。用数字走一遍，设患病率1%：10万人里1000人患病，其中990人检出阳性；99000人没病，约4950人假阳性。阳性共约5940人，真患病的只有990人，所以 P(患病|阳性)=990/5940≈16.7%。直觉：没病的人基数太大，假阳性在数量上压过了真阳性。先验（患病率）在这里起决定作用——同样的检测，放在患病率高的医院，阳性结果就靠谱得多。
answers.d06: A cache keeps a copy of data close by so you don't pay to fetch or recompute it on every request. Invalidation is the rule for throwing that copy away when the real data changes. Example: a product's price changes in the database, but the page was cached and still shows $20 — until that copy is invalidated, every visitor sees a wrong price. The cache bought speed by serving stale data. It's famously hard because one database row can feed many cached pages across many servers, and you must find and drop exactly the right copies, every single time. Common compromises: give each copy a time-to-live and accept a few minutes of staleness, or explicitly delete the copy when the data is written. Every choice trades freshness against speed and complexity — a cache with no invalidation strategy isn't an optimization; it's a bug waiting to surface.
answers.d07: 两个量一起变是相关；一个的改变引起另一个的改变，才是因果。看一组真实现象：冰淇淋销量与溺水人数同涨同跌，相关很强。直接下结论『吃冰淇淋导致溺水』就错了：背后有个共同原因——天热。热既让人多买冰淇淋，也让人多去游泳，溺水随之增多。这种藏在后面的共同原因叫混杂变量，它能让毫无因果的两个量表现出强相关。区分的办法是把共同原因控制住：只看同样气温的日子，若两者的相关消失，说明原相关是季节带来的。更硬的手段是随机实验：随机分组强制一组吃冰淇淋、一组不吃，气温等其他条件被随机拉平，剩下的差异才能归于冰淇淋——当然这个实验不会有人做。也要留意反方向：相关并非与因果无关，它常是因果的线索，只是单凭相关定不了方向和机制；而在这个例子里，相关确实完全来自混杂。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth earns growth: each period's gain is computed on everything accumulated so far, not just the start. Put $100 at 10% per year: after one year you have 110; after two, 10% applies to 110, giving 121. After n years it's 100 × 1.1ⁿ. That exponent is the mechanism — gains are reinvested, so the same rate acts on an ever-larger base. This is why the starting amount matters. Two people earning the same 10%, one from $100 and one from $200, keep the same ratio, but the dollar gap widens yearly: after 30 years, about $1,745 versus $3,490 — a gap that began as $100. Change the rate instead: at 5%, the same $100 reaches only about $432 in 30 years. Both rate and time sit in the exponent, which is why starting early usually beats starting big.
answers.v01: 过拟合是模型把训练数据里的噪声和细节也当成了规律：训练数据上表现很好，换新数据就明显变差。打个比方：你请人记住去车站的路线，他连『经过第三棵歪树后左转』都背下来，走这条路没问题，换一条路就抓瞎——因为歪树不是规律，『路口右转』才是。机器学习里是同样的结构：一个复杂模型在训练集上准确率98%，新样本上只有70%，这28个点的落差就是过拟合的信号——模型背了题，没学会规律。为什么会这样：模型太灵活而数据太少，它有能力把每个训练样本都拟合到位，包括纯属偶然的起伏。对策顺着原因来：更多数据、更简单的模型，以及用没参与训练的验证集来检验。判断模型好不好，看的永远是新数据上的表现，不是它在训练集上的分数。
answers.v02: Search for 'jaguar': the engine returns 10 results. Six are about the car (relevant); four are big cats or a football club. Four more relevant pages exist but weren't returned. Precision answers: of what was shown, how much was right? 6/10 = 60%. Recall answers: of everything relevant that exists, how much was found? 6/10 = 60% here too, but they are different questions — precision judges the returned list; recall judges the search against all relevant documents. The two trade off: return only the single most certain result and precision may hit 100% while recall falls to 25%; dump everything and recall hits 100% while precision collapses. Which matters more depends on the task: legal discovery tolerates junk (recall first); a quick answer box doesn't (precision first). A system can score well on one and badly on the other.
answers.v03: 自然选择改变的是种群中不同特征的比例，不需要任何个体『努力变强』。机制分三步：个体之间存在遗传差异；这些差异影响各自留下后代的数量；留下后代多的差异，在下一代种群中的占比升高。如此逐代筛下去，种群的整体特征就改变了。例子：一片常被割草机修剪的草地，高茎个体一被割就开不了花、结不了籽，矮茎的能照常繁殖，下一代矮茎比例升高——不是草『努力往矮里长』，变异本来就随机存在，割草机只是让矮茎恰好留下更多后代。个体终生不变，变的是种群的构成。条件变化：停止割草后，高茎在争夺阳光上占优，比例又会回升——选择方向随环境翻转。常见误读是『用进废退』式的主动努力：长颈鹿不是伸脖子伸出来的，是脖子长的个体留下更多后代。
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent when doing it any number of times has the same effect as doing it once. Distributed systems care because networks fail ambiguously: a request may time out with no answer, and you can't tell whether the server never got it or already completed it. Retrying is the natural response — but it's only safe if a repeat does no extra harm. Contrast two calls: set_price(99) is idempotent, since a retry just sets 99 again; add_to_balance(10) is not, since a retry after a successful first attempt pays the customer twice. The standard fix is an idempotency key: the client generates a unique ID per logical operation and sends it with every retry. The server records processed keys and, on a repeat, returns the stored result instead of redoing the work — turning an unknown outcome into a safely repeated one.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量的是结果揭晓之前你有多不确定，公式 H = −Σ pᵢ·log₂ pᵢ，单位是比特。为什么均匀分布最不确定：抛均匀硬币，正反各0.5，揭晓前你完全没法偏爱任何一个答案；一旦正面概率变成0.9，『猜正面』就已经是很可靠的预测，不确定性随之下降。代入数字：均匀硬币 H = 0.5×1 + 0.5×1 = 1 比特；0.9/0.1 的硬币 H ≈ 0.47 比特；某个结果概率为1时 H = 0，毫无悬念。比特可以读成『平均至少需要几个是非题才能确定结果』：概率越不均匀，先问高概率项越省问题，所以熵更低。公式写法也对得上这个直觉：对数把概率换算成需要的问题数，乘 pᵢ 再求和是按各结果出现的可能性取平均。注意这是揭晓前的平均不确定性，不是某一次结果的意外程度。
answers.v06: Deadlock is a standstill where several processes each hold a resource the others are waiting for, so nobody can move. Example: transaction A locks file 1, transaction B locks file 2. A then asks for file 2 — waits. B asks for file 1 — waits. Each holds exactly what the other needs; both wait forever. Four conditions must all hold: resources are exclusive, holders keep them while waiting for more, nothing can be forcibly taken back, and the waits form a circle. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible. Easiest to break is the circle: have every transaction request files in one global order (file 1 before file 2), so B can never hold 2 while waiting for 1. Alternatives: release held locks before requesting new ones, or abort on timeout and retry. The same picture shows up with threads and mutexes, and with database row locks.
answers.v07: 判断公共物品看两条性质：非排他——没法阻止没付钱的人享用；消费无竞争——多一人享用，别人享用的并不减少。路灯两条都占：挡不住路人借光，一个人走夜路也不消耗别处的光。由此产生搭便车：反正不付钱也照样有路灯，理性的个体就不愿出钱。麻烦在于人人这样想——路灯明明对整条街价值很高，自愿凑钱却总凑不齐，市场按『谁付钱谁享用』的逻辑干脆不供给，这就是供给不足。对比面包：不付钱吃不到（排他），多吃一口别人就少吃一口（竞争），所以面包市场供给得很好。条件变化能改变归类：收费电视靠加密把未付费者挡在外面，非排他被技术破掉，就能市场化。现实对策是用税收统一供给国防、海堤这类物品，或靠社群规范约束搭便车者。先查两条性质，再判断由谁供给。
answers.v08: Little's law: L = λW. L is the average number of customers in the system, λ the average arrival rate, W the average time each spends in the system. In steady state it holds no matter how arrivals scatter or how you order the queue. The reason is bookkeeping, not luck: whatever comes in must flow out, so the stock inside equals the flow rate times how long each unit stays — like a bathtub where inflow × drain-time fixes the water level. Numbers: 10 customers arrive per minute and each spends 4 minutes inside, so on average L = 40 customers are present. It's a measuring tool: observe any two quantities, infer the third. Cut wait time to 2 minutes at the same arrival rate and the crowd inside halves to 20. The limit matters: in overload, arrivals outpace service, the queue grows without bound, and these stable averages no longer exist.
